passages.text: This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.
passages.sermon:
This saying is trustworthy.
Anyone can aspire to be an overseer.
An overseer is a leader in the church.
If someone wants to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.
passages.original: Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος εἴ τις ἐπισκοπῆς ὀρέγεται καλοῦ ἔργου ἐπιθυμεῖ

passages.text: An overseer, then, must be above reproach, the husband of but one wife, temperate, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach, not dependent on wine, not violent but gentle, peaceable, and free of the love of money.
passages.sermon:
An overseer leads the church of God.
An overseer must be above reproach.
He must be the husband of only one wife.
He must be temperate.
He must be self-controlled.
He must be respectable.
He must be hospitable.
He must be able to teach.
He must not depend on wine.
He must not be violent.
He must be gentle.
He must be peaceable.
He must not love money.
passages.original: δεῖ οὖν τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ἀνεπίλημπτον εἶναι μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἄνδρα νηφάλιον σώφρονα κόσμιον φιλόξενον διδακτικόν μὴ πάροινον μὴ πλήκτην ἀλλὰ ἐπιεικῆ ἄμαχον ἀφιλάργυρον

passages.text: An overseer must manage his own household well and keep his children under control, with complete dignity.
passages.sermon:
An overseer leads his own household well.
He manages his family with care.
He keeps his children under control.
He does this with complete dignity.
passages.original: τοῦ ἰδίου οἴκου καλῶς προϊστάμενον τέκνα ἔχοντα ἐν ὑποταγῇ μετὰ πάσης σεμνότητος

passages.text: For if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how can he care for the church of God?
passages.sermon:
An overseer must manage his own household well.
He must know how to lead his family.
If a man does not know how to manage his own household, he cannot care for the church of God.
Managing a household shows ability to care for the church.
Caring for the church of God requires proven leadership at home.
passages.original: εἰ δέ τις τοῦ ἰδίου οἴκου προστῆναι οὐκ οἶδεν πῶς ἐκκλησίας Θεοῦ ἐπιμελήσεται

passages.text: He must not be a recent convert, or he may become conceited and fall under the same condemnation as the devil.
passages.sermon:
An overseer must not be a recent convert.
A recent convert is someone who is new to the faith.
If an overseer is a recent convert, he may become proud.
If he becomes proud, he may fall under the same judgment as the devil.
passages.original: μὴ νεόφυτον ἵνα μὴ τυφωθεὶς εἰς κρίμα ἐμπέσῃ τοῦ διαβόλου

passages.text: Furthermore, he must have a good reputation with outsiders, so that he will not fall into disgrace and into the snare of the devil.
passages.sermon: A church leader must have a good reputation with people outside the church.\r\nThis good reputation protects him from falling into disgrace.\r\nIt also keeps him from falling into the trap of the devil.
passages.original: δεῖ δὲ καὶ μαρτυρίαν καλὴν ἔχειν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔξωθεν ἵνα μὴ εἰς ὀνειδισμὸν ἐμπέσῃ καὶ παγίδα τοῦ διαβόλου

passages.text: Deacons likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued or given to much wine or greedy for money.
passages.sermon:
Deacons must be dignified.
Deacons must not speak with double meanings.
Deacons must not drink too much wine.
Deacons must not be greedy for money.
passages.original: Διακόνους ὡσαύτως σεμνούς μὴ διλόγους μὴ οἴνῳ πολλῷ προσέχοντας μὴ αἰσχροκερδεῖς

passages.text: They must hold to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.
passages.sermon: Deacons must hold to the mystery of the faith.\r\nThey must have a clear conscience.
passages.original: ἔχοντας τὸ μυστήριον τῆς πίστεως ἐν καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει

passages.text: Additionally, they must first be tested. Then, if they are above reproach, let them serve as deacons.
passages.sermon: Deacons must first be tested.\r\nIf they are above reproach, they may serve as deacons.
passages.original: καὶ οὗτοι δὲ δοκιμαζέσθωσαν πρῶτον εἶτα διακονείτωσαν ἀνέγκλητοι ὄντες

passages.text: In the same way, the women must be dignified, not slanderers, but temperate and faithful in all things.
passages.sermon:
The women must be dignified.
They must not be slanderers.
They must be temperate.
They must be faithful in all things.
passages.original: Γυναῖκας ὡσαύτως σεμνάς μὴ διαβόλους νηφαλίους πιστὰς ἐν πᾶσιν

passages.text: A deacon must be the husband of but one wife, a good manager of his children and of his own household.
passages.sermon: A deacon must be a man who has only one wife.\r\nA deacon must manage his children well.\r\nA deacon must manage his own household well.
passages.original: Διάκονοι ἔστωσαν μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἄνδρες τέκνων καλῶς προϊστάμενοι καὶ τῶν ἰδίων οἴκων

passages.text: For those who have served well as deacons acquire for themselves a high standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
A deacon is a servant in the church of the living God.
Some deacons serve well.
Those who serve well as deacons gain a good standing for themselves.
They also gain great confidence.
Their confidence is in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
passages.original: οἱ γὰρ καλῶς διακονήσαντες βαθμὸν ἑαυτοῖς καλὸν περιποιοῦνται καὶ πολλὴν παρρησίαν ἐν πίστει τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Although I hope to come to you soon, I am writing you these things in case I am delayed, so that you will know how each one must conduct himself in God’s household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter to Timothy.
Paul hopes to visit Timothy soon.
Paul may be delayed.
Paul writes these instructions in case he cannot come quickly.
Paul wants Timothy to know how to behave in God’s household.
God’s household is the church.
The church belongs to the living God.
The church is the pillar of the truth.
The church is the foundation of the truth.
passages.original: Ταῦτά σοι γράφω ἐλπίζων ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ ἐν τάχει ἐὰν δὲ βραδύνω ἵνα εἰδῇς πῶς δεῖ ἐν οἴκῳ Θεοῦ ἀναστρέφεσθαι ἥτις ἐστὶν ἐκκλησία Θεοῦ ζῶντος στῦλος καὶ ἑδραίωμα τῆς ἀληθείας

passages.text: By common confession, the mystery of godliness is great: He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among the nations, was believed in throughout the world, was taken up in glory.
passages.sermon:
The mystery of godliness is very great.
Everyone agrees about this.
Jesus Christ is the subject of this mystery.
He appeared in the flesh.
The Spirit vindicated Him.
Angels saw Him.
People proclaimed Him among the nations.
People in the world believed in Him.
God took Him up in glory.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁμολογουμένως μέγα ἐστὶν τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας μυστήριον Ὃς ἐφανερώθη ἐν σαρκί ἐδικαιώθη ἐν πνεύματι ὤφθη ἀγγέλοις ἐκηρύχθη ἐν ἔθνεσιν ἐπιστεύθη ἐν κόσμῳ ἀνελήμφθη ἐν δόξῃ
